s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent syncope with palpitations and transient loss of consciousness
salient_findings: Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia during presyncope episode
Diffuse stenosis in proximal to mid-LAD and mid-right coronary artery
key_facts: Reported palpitation and amaurosis before loss of consciousness
Previous episode of syncope 1 month prior
Vital signs: blood pressure 125/96 mm Hg, pulse rate 81 beats/min, respiratory rate 18 breaths/min, and oxygen saturation 99% under ambient air
Normal laboratory tests, including blood glucose, electrolytes, D-dimer, troponin I, and N-terminal pro–B-type natriuretic peptide
Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia recorded during 24-hour Holter monitoring
50% to 90% diffuse stenosis in proximal to mid-LAD
Minimum lumen area of 5.92 mm2 in proximal LAD, with plaque burden of 74%

raw.rationale: The patient has significant coronary artery stenosis, including 50% to 90% diffuse stenosis in the proximal to mid-LAD and 80% stenosis in the mid-right coronary artery, which could lead to reduced blood flow to the heart, causing symptoms such as syncope and palpitations.

rejected.label: Long QT syndrome
rejected.why: The QTc interval of 403 milliseconds is within the normal range for most adults, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Acute coronary syndrome
rejected.why: There is no evidence of acute myocardial infarction or unstable angina, as troponin I levels are normal and there are no symptoms of chest pain or shortness of breath.

rejected.label: Brugada syndrome
rejected.why: There is no characteristic ST-segment elevation in leads V1-V3 on the electrocardiogram, which is a hallmark of Brugada syndrome.

rejected.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: There is no evidence of right ventricular dysfunction or fibrofatty replacement on the transthoracic echocardiography, which is characteristic of this condition.
